description: Sample FAQ knowledge base for the CodeAlpha FAQ Chatbot. Add new entries to the "faqs" list; no Python changes are needed.

faqs.question: What is this chatbot?
faqs.answer: I'm an FAQ chatbot. I answer common questions about technology, programming, AI basics, education and student life by finding the closest match in a curated list of questions. I don't generate new answers, so I can only help with topics in my knowledge base.

faqs.question: How does this chatbot work?
alternative_questions: How does this chatbot understand my question?
faqs.answer: Your question is cleaned up (lowercased, punctuation and filler words removed) and converted into TF-IDF vectors. Cosine similarity then compares it with every FAQ question, and the best match is returned if its score passes a confidence threshold. Otherwise you get a fallback message with suggestions.

faqs.question: Is this chatbot powered by ChatGPT or a large language model?
faqs.answer: No. This is a retrieval-based chatbot built with Python, Flask and scikit-learn. It selects a pre-written answer using TF-IDF and cosine similarity; it does not generate text or call any external AI service.

faqs.question: Why didn't the chatbot understand my question?
alternative_questions: What are the limitations of this chatbot?
Why do I get a fallback answer?
faqs.answer: The chatbot only knows the questions stored in its FAQ file. If your wording is very different, or the topic isn't covered, the best match scores below the confidence threshold and you get a fallback reply. Try rephrasing with keywords, choosing a topic filter, or using one of the suggested questions.

faqs.question: How can new questions be added to the chatbot?
alternative_questions: How do I add a new FAQ?
How do I update the knowledge base?
faqs.answer: Open data/faqs.json and add an object to the "faqs" list with a unique id, a category, a question, an answer and optional alternative_questions. Restart the app and the new entry is picked up automatically. No Python changes are needed.

faqs.question: Does the chatbot store my messages?
faqs.answer: The server does not save the text of your messages. It only keeps anonymous counters, such as how often each FAQ was matched, and these reset when the server restarts. Your conversation is kept in your browser's session storage so it survives a page refresh, and it disappears when you close the tab or press Clear.

faqs.question: Hello
faqs.answer: Hello! I can answer questions about technology, programming, AI fundamentals, education and student life. Try one of the suggested questions or type your own.

faqs.question: Thank you
faqs.answer: You're welcome! Ask me another question any time.

faqs.question: What is the internet?
faqs.answer: The internet is a global network of interconnected computers and networks that exchange data using shared rules called protocols, such as TCP/IP. It carries services like email, file transfer and the World Wide Web.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the internet and the World Wide Web?
alternative_questions: Is the web the same as the internet?
faqs.answer: The internet is the underlying network infrastructure, while the World Wide Web is one service that runs on it: a collection of web pages and resources accessed through browsers using HTTP or HTTPS. Email and online gaming also use the internet but are not part of the web.

faqs.question: What is cloud computing?
alternative_questions: What does the cloud mean in technology?
faqs.answer: Cloud computing means using computing resources such as servers, storage, databases and software over the internet from a provider, instead of owning and maintaining the hardware yourself. You typically pay for what you use and can scale up or down as needed.

faqs.question: What is an IP address?
faqs.answer: An IP address is a numerical label that identifies a device on a network so data can be sent to the right place. IPv4 addresses look like 192.168.1.1, and the newer IPv6 format uses longer hexadecimal addresses.

faqs.question: How do I create a strong password?
faqs.answer: Use a long password or passphrase (12 or more characters), avoid personal details and common words, and never reuse the same password on different sites. A password manager can generate and store unique passwords, and two-factor authentication adds another layer of protection.

faqs.question: What is an operating system?
faqs.answer: An operating system (OS) is the core software that manages a computer's hardware and lets applications run. Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS are common examples.

faqs.question: What is open-source software?
faqs.answer: Open-source software has source code that anyone can read, use, modify and share under a license that permits it. Examples include Linux, Python and Flask. The license still defines the exact rules you must follow.

faqs.question: What is HTTPS?
alternative_questions: What does the padlock in the browser mean?
faqs.answer: HTTPS is HTTP secured with TLS encryption, which protects data travelling between your browser and a website from being read or tampered with. The padlock icon means the connection is encrypted, but it does not guarantee that the site itself is trustworthy.

faqs.question: What is an internship and why is it useful?
faqs.answer: An internship is a short-term work placement where you apply your skills to real tasks and learn how a profession operates. It builds practical experience, a portfolio and professional contacts, and it often helps when applying for jobs.

faqs.question: How do I write a good resume as a student?
alternative_questions: What should I put on my resume with no experience?
faqs.answer: Keep it to one page and lead with a short summary, education, skills and projects. Describe each project by what you built, the tools you used and what it does, and only list skills you can talk about confidently. Proofread carefully and tailor it to each role.

faqs.question: How can I study more effectively?
alternative_questions: How do I remember what I learn?
faqs.answer: Active recall (testing yourself) and spaced repetition (reviewing at growing intervals) are usually more effective than rereading notes. Study in focused sessions with short breaks, practice with problems, and explain concepts in your own words.

faqs.question: What free resources can I use to learn programming?
alternative_questions: Where can I learn coding for free?
Best free websites to learn to code
faqs.answer: Good free options include Harvard's CS50 lectures, freeCodeCamp, MDN Web Docs for web development, and the official Python tutorial at python.org. Pick one and build small projects as you go.

faqs.question: How do I prepare for a technical interview?
alternative_questions: How to prepare for an internship interview
faqs.answer: Review the basics of the language and the topics in the role, practice solving problems out loud, and be ready to explain your own projects in detail, including design decisions and trade-offs. Mock interviews with a friend help, and it is fine to ask clarifying questions.

faqs.question: What is Python?
faqs.answer: Python is a high-level, general-purpose programming language known for its readable syntax. It is widely used for web development, automation, data analysis and machine learning, and it has a large ecosystem of libraries.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a list and a tuple in Python?
faqs.answer: Lists are mutable, so you can add, remove or change items after creating them, while tuples are immutable and cannot be changed once created. Tuples are often used for fixed collections and can be dictionary keys when their items are hashable.

faqs.question: What is a virtual environment in Python?
alternative_questions: How do I create a virtual environment?
faqs.answer: A virtual environment is an isolated Python setup with its own installed packages, so different projects don't conflict. On Windows you can create one with `py -m venv .venv` and install packages with `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt`.

faqs.question: What is Git and why should I use it?
faqs.answer: Git is a version control system that records changes to your files over time. It lets you review history, undo mistakes, work on features in branches and collaborate with others without overwriting each other's work.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Git and GitHub?
alternative_questions: Is GitHub the same as Git?
faqs.answer: Git is the tool that tracks changes on your computer. GitHub is an online service that hosts Git repositories and adds collaboration features such as pull requests and issues. You can use Git without GitHub, but GitHub makes sharing code easier.

faqs.question: What is an API?
faqs.answer: An API (Application Programming Interface) is a defined way for one piece of software to request data or actions from another. Web APIs usually receive HTTP requests and return data, often as JSON. This chatbot's web page talks to its Flask backend that way.

faqs.question: What is Flask?
alternative_questions: Tell me about the Flask framework
faqs.answer: Flask is a lightweight Python web framework for building websites and APIs. It provides routing and request handling and leaves other choices, such as databases, to you, which makes it popular for small and medium projects.

faqs.question: What is JSON?
faqs.answer: JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is a text format for structured data that uses objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans and null. It is human-readable and supported by almost every programming language, which is why it is common for APIs and configuration files.

faqs.question: What is object-oriented programming?
faqs.answer: Object-oriented programming (OOP) organizes code around objects that bundle data (attributes) and behavior (methods), defined by classes. Core ideas include encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and abstraction.

faqs.question: How do I fix errors in my code?
alternative_questions: How do I debug a program?
My code is not working, what should I do?
faqs.answer: Read the error message from the bottom up to find the error type and the exact line, then reproduce the problem with the smallest example you can. Use print statements or a debugger to check values, change one thing at a time, and search the exact message when you are stuck.

faqs.question: What is artificial intelligence?
faqs.answer: Artificial intelligence (AI) is the field of building computer systems that perform tasks normally associated with human intelligence, such as understanding language, recognizing images or making decisions.

faqs.question: What is machine learning?
faqs.answer: Machine learning is a branch of AI where algorithms learn patterns from data instead of relying only on hand-written rules. The trained model can then make predictions or decisions on new data.

faqs.question: What is the difference between AI, machine learning and deep learning?
alternative_questions: AI vs ML vs deep learning
Is deep learning part of machine learning?
faqs.answer: AI is the broad goal of building intelligent machines, machine learning is a subset of AI that learns from data, and deep learning is a subset of machine learning that uses neural networks with many layers.

faqs.question: What is natural language processing?
alternative_questions: How do computers understand human language?
faqs.answer: Natural language processing (NLP) is the area of AI that lets computers work with human language. Typical tasks include translation, sentiment analysis, chatbots and search. Techniques range from simple word counts to large neural language models.

faqs.question: What is TF-IDF?
faqs.answer: TF-IDF (term frequency-inverse document frequency) scores how important a word is to a text compared with a collection of texts. Words that appear often in one text but rarely elsewhere get high weights, while very common words get low weights.

faqs.question: What is cosine similarity?
alternative_questions: How do you measure similarity between texts?
faqs.answer: Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors: 1 means they point the same way and 0 means they share nothing. For text, the vectors are built from word weights, so it compares wording overlap. It does not check whether either statement is true.

faqs.question: What is the difference between supervised and unsupervised learning?
faqs.answer: Supervised learning trains on labeled examples (inputs with known correct outputs) to predict labels for new data, as in spam detection. Unsupervised learning finds structure in unlabeled data, such as grouping similar customers with clustering.

faqs.question: What is overfitting in machine learning?
alternative_questions: Why does my model do well on training data but badly on new data?
faqs.answer: Overfitting happens when a model learns the training data too closely, including its noise, so it performs poorly on new data. Common remedies include more data, simpler models, regularization, cross-validation and early stopping.

faqs.question: What is a neural network?
alternative_questions: How does a neural network work?
faqs.answer: A neural network is a model made of layers of connected units (neurons) that transform inputs into outputs. It learns by adjusting the connection weights to reduce prediction error, usually with gradient descent.

faqs.question: Which programming language should I learn first?
alternative_questions: Python or Java for a beginner?
faqs.answer: Python is a popular first choice because its syntax is easy to read and it is useful in many areas. The best language depends on your goals (web, mobile, games or data), so choose one that fits and focus on understanding programming concepts, which carry over between languages.

faqs.question: How do I build a portfolio project?
alternative_questions: What projects should I put in my portfolio?
faqs.answer: Pick a small problem you care about, build a complete working version, then polish it with tests, a clear README and screenshots. Ideas include a to-do app, a quiz game, a weather dashboard or an FAQ chatbot like this one. A finished, well-documented project that you can explain beats several half-finished ones.

faqs.question: How much should I practice coding every day?
alternative_questions: How many hours should I code daily?
How do I stay consistent with learning to code?
faqs.answer: There is no fixed number, and consistency matters more than long marathons. Even 30 to 60 focused minutes most days, spent building things rather than only watching tutorials, usually works better than an occasional long session.

faqs.question: How do I upload my project to GitHub?
alternative_questions: How do I push code to GitHub?
Steps to publish a project on GitHub
faqs.answer: Create an empty repository on GitHub, then in your project folder run `git init`, `git add .`, `git commit -m "Initial commit"`, `git branch -M main`, `git remote add origin <your-repo-url>` and `git push -u origin main`. Check your .gitignore first so secrets and virtual environments are not uploaded.

faqs.question: How do I balance studies and personal projects?
alternative_questions: How do I manage my time better?
faqs.answer: Plan your week with fixed study blocks, set small project goals (for example one feature per session) and protect time for rest. Prioritize deadlines, avoid multitasking and review your plan weekly.

faqs.question: How do I stay motivated when learning gets hard?
alternative_questions: I feel stuck while learning to code
How do I avoid giving up on a difficult subject?
faqs.answer: Break the topic into small tasks you can finish in one sitting and track your progress. Struggling is a normal part of learning. Take breaks, ask for help in communities or from mentors, and revisit earlier projects to see how far you have come.
